mainTopic: Fuels exempt from the רוב rule, the end of פרק יציאות השבת, and the opening of במה מדליקין on forbidden wicks and fuels
overview: This amud finishes the first פרק of מסכת שבת and begins the second. First the גמרא lists fuels that do not need the fire to catch 'most' (רוב) of them before שבת: loose reeds, pits in baskets, quick-burning bonfires, and the 'wood of בבל', which רב יוסף and רמי בר אבא each identify. Then the פרק ends with the הדרן. The new פרק opens with the famous משנה 'במה מדליקין', which lists wicks and fuels that may not be used for the שבת lamp. It ends with a dispute about boiled tallow between נחום המדי and the חכמים. The גמרא then goes through the משנה word by word, identifying each material, such as לכש, חוסן, כלך, אידן and the green moss. Along the way there are challenges, stories about רבין and אביי, and a refutation of רבין about כלך. A ברייתא adds wool and hair, and another shows that from זפת onward the משנה lists fuels, not wicks. So wax may be used on a wick but not as fuel.

steps.title: רב כהנא on reeds and pits
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא rules that bundled reeds need רוב and loose reeds do not. Loose pits need רוב, but pits placed in baskets do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said: Reeds that were tied together need the fire to catch most of them. Reeds that were not tied do not need most. Pits need most. If they were put into baskets, they do not need most.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא gives two pairs of cases. In each pair, the way the fuel is arranged decides whether the fire must catch 'most' of it before שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The basic rule of the משנה is that a fire must catch רוב of its fuel before שבת. רב כהנא shows that the arrangement of the fuel matters. Tied-up reeds burn worse than loose ones, so only the tied bundle needs רוב. Pits burn poorly when loose, but when put into baskets the whole basket burns well, so they no longer need רוב.

keyTerms.meaning: Most / the majority. Here it means the fire must catch most of the fuel.
He tied them into a bundle
Pits or seeds used as fuel
Woven baskets made of palm leaves

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume that tying reeds together makes them burn better. Here the bundle is the case that is stricter and needs רוב.

phrases.english: Reeds that one tied together require most [to catch fire],
if he did not tie them, they do not require most.
if he placed them in woven baskets, they do not require most.
phrases.notes: In the basket, the fire takes hold well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion on the daf about which fuels need רוב, following the statement of רב הונא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bundled reeds and loose pits need רוב. Loose reeds and pits in baskets do not.

steps.title: Four bonfires that do not need most
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף teaches a ברייתא: bonfires of pitch, sulfur, cheese and fat do not need רוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף taught: Four kinds of bonfires do not need most to be burning: one of pitch, one of sulfur, one of cheese, and one of fat.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף quotes a ברייתא that lists four fuels which do not need the fire to catch most of them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These materials catch fire very quickly and keep burning by themselves. Once the fire touches them, nobody will need to stoke them on שבת. So the reason for requiring רוב does not apply to them.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught a ברייתא (a teaching from the תנאים)

phrases.english: Four bonfires do not require most [to catch fire]:
and of [dry] cheese, and of fat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds more exceptions to the רוב rule, this time from a ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Fuels that catch easily (pitch, sulfur, cheese, fat) do not need רוב.

steps.title: Another ברייתא adds straw and twigs
steps.stepSummary: A different ברייתא adds bonfires of straw and of gathered twigs to the list.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא taught: Also bonfires of straw and of gathered twigs do not need most.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that adds two more fuels to רב יוסף's list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Straw and small twigs gathered from the field are thin and dry, so they catch fire at once. The word אף ('also') shows this ברייתא is adding to the earlier list, not arguing with it.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
Twigs and stubble raked up from the field

phrases.english: It was taught in a baraita:
Also [bonfires] of straw and of rakings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the list of exceptions from step 2.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Straw and raked twigs also do not need רוב.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן on Babylonian wood
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that the wood of בבל does not need רוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: The wood of בבל does not need most to be burning.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן adds one more exception, a kind of wood used in בבל. He does not say which wood he means, and this sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the earlier examples, this ruling is unclear. 'Babylonian wood' could mean several things. The גמרא will now try to identify it.

phrases.aramaic: עֵצִים שֶׁל בָּבֶל אֵין צְרִיכִין רוֹב.
phrases.english: Babylonian wood does not require most [to catch fire].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new exception whose meaning will be clarified.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Babylonian wood does not need רוב.

steps.title: רב יוסף asks which wood is meant
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף challenges: it cannot mean wood slivers. עולא said even a wick needs רוב, so slivers surely need רוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף objected: What wood is this? If you say it means wood slivers, think about this. עולא said that even with a wick, one must light most of the part sticking out. Is there any question that slivers need most?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף asks what 'Babylonian wood' means. He rejects the obvious guess, wood slivers, with a קל וחומר from עולא's rule about a wick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא taught that even a thin wick must burn on most of its exposed part. Slivers of wood catch fire less easily than a wick, so they would surely need רוב. Therefore רבי יוחנן cannot be talking about slivers.

keyTerms.meaning: Wood slivers used for fire and light
Is it even a question? (meaning: certainly)

steps.confusionAlert: 'סילתי מבעיא' does not mean slivers are exempt. It means slivers obviously need רוב, which is why רבי יוחנן cannot mean slivers.

phrases.english: now, regarding a wick, Ulla said
one who lights must light most of what sticks out,
is it even a question regarding slivers?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקִיף לַהּ רַב יוֹסֵף מַאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the identity of the wood in רבי יוחנן's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that 'Babylonian wood' means slivers.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: if a wick needs רוב, slivers certainly do. So רבי יוחנן's exemption cannot refer to them.

steps.title: רב יוסף: it means a cedar branch
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that רבי יוחנן means a branch of a cedar tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוסף said: It means a cedar branch.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives his own answer. The wood is a cedar branch, which burns very well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A cedar branch is full of resin, so once it catches it keeps burning by itself. That explains why it does not need רוב, while slivers do.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (rejects the earlier idea and gives a new one)

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5 after rejecting slivers.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means a cedar branch, which burns easily.

steps.title: רמי בר אבא: it means זאזא
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר אבא gives a different identification: זאזא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר אבא said: It means זאזא.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא offers another answer to what 'Babylonian wood' is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רמי בר אבא agrees that the wood must be one that catches fire easily, but he names a different plant, זאזא (Sefaria: hyssop). The two answers do not disagree on the law, only on which wood it is.

keyTerms.meaning: A plant used as fuel (Sefaria: hyssop)

steps.whatToRemember: The basic rule needs fire on רוב of the fuel before שבת. Fuels that catch fire easily, or are arranged so they burn well, are exceptions.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternative answer to the same question that רב יוסף answered.

steps.title: הדרן — Closing יציאות השבת
steps.stepSummary: The closing formula of the first פרק of מסכת שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, יציאות השבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the first פרק, יציאות השבת, with the traditional farewell line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הדרן is a statement of love for the learning and a promise to come back to it. The second פרק, במה מדליקין, comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you (said when finishing a פרק)
Name of the first פרק of מסכת שבת

phrases.english: We shall return to you, Yetziot HaShabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the chapter.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: End of the first פרק of מסכת שבת.

steps.title: The new chapter opens: forbidden wicks
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks what may and may not be used for the שבת lamp, then lists six wick materials that are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: With what may we light the שבת lamp, and with what may we not light it? We may not light with לכש, חוסן, כלך, פתילת האידן, פתילת המדבר, or the green moss on the surface of water.
steps.whatsHappening: A brand-new פרק begins with a question and a list of wick materials that may not be used for the שבת lamp.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These materials do not burn well, so the flame flickers. The worry is that a person might adjust the lamp on שבת, which is forbidden. This first half of the list is all about wicks.

keyTerms.meaning: A cedar material (the גמרא will explain it)

steps.confusionAlert: Step 8 was the הדרן closing the first פרק. This is the opening of a NEW פרק, not a continuation of the cedar-wood discussion, even though cedar comes up again soon.
steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is the famous 'במה מדליקין' that many communities say on Friday night, so its words are familiar even if their meanings are not.

phrases.english: Mishnah: With what may one light
phrases.notes: Opening words and title of the new chapter

phrases.english: and with what may one not light?
One may not light with cedar bast (lekhesh),
nor with ḥosen, nor with kalakh,
nor with the green moss on the surface of the water,

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ בַּמֶּה מַדְלִיקִין וּבַמָּה אֵין מַדְלִיקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new perek right after the הדרן in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These six wick materials may not be used for the שבת lamp.

steps.title: Forbidden fuels for the שבת lamp
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues its list with six fuels that may not be used: pitch, wax, castor oil, burnt oil, tail fat, and tallow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Nor with pitch, nor with wax, nor with castor oil, nor with burnt oil, nor with tail fat, nor with tallow.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves from wicks to oils and fuels and lists six that are not allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list now covers the fuel inside the lamp, not the wick. Some of these fuels burn poorly. שמן שריפה is a special case: it is תרומה oil that became impure and must be burned. The final item, חלב, sets up the disagreement that comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Impure תרומה oil that must be burned

phrases.english: nor with pitch, nor with wax,
nor with oil designated for burning,
nor with sheep's tail fat, nor with tallow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list, switching from wicks to fuels.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: These six fuels may not be used for the שבת lamp.

steps.title: נחום המדי permits boiled tallow
steps.stepSummary: נחום המדי says that tallow which has been boiled may be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: נחום המדי says: We may light with boiled tallow.
steps.whatsHappening: A תנא named נחום המדי disagrees with the last item on the list and allows tallow if it was boiled first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה had just said 'not with חלב.' נחום המדי holds that boiling changes the tallow so it burns well. In his view, there is then no reason to worry.

phrases.english: One may light with boiled tallow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Makes an exception to the ban on חלב in step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Boiled tallow is permitted for lighting.

steps.title: The חכמים forbid tallow either way
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say that tallow is forbidden whether or not it was boiled.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: Both boiled and unboiled tallow, we may not light with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים reject נחום המדי's exception and keep tallow fully forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the חכמים' view, boiling does not make a difference. The ban on חלב in the משנה stays in place with no exception.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה lists forbidden wicks, then forbidden fuels. It ends with a dispute: נחום המדי permits boiled tallow, while the חכמים forbid all tallow.

phrases.english: one may not light with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with נחום המדי in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All tallow is forbidden for lighting, boiled or not.

steps.title: Defining לכש as a cedar branch
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins explaining the משנה's words and says that לכש is a branch of a cedar tree.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: לכש is a cedar branch.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts translating the unfamiliar words of the משנה, beginning with לכש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many of these materials were unknown in בבל, so the גמרא acts like a dictionary. This definition sets up the question that comes right after it.

phrases.english: Gemara: Lekhesh is a branch of the cedar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins explaining the first word on the משנה's wick list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: לכש is the cedar branch.

steps.title: Wood cannot be a wick
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: a cedar branch is just wood, so how could it be a wick?
steps.simpleTranslation: A cedar branch is just ordinary wood!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the definition it just gave, because wood is not wick material.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's list is about wicks, which must be soft and fibrous. A plain wooden branch does not fit that category, so the definition seems wrong.

phrases.english: A cedar branch is mere wood!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the definition in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: The identification of לכש as a cedar branch.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A wick must be fibrous, and wood is not, so a branch cannot be what the משנה means.

steps.title: The woolly layer under the bark
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה means the soft, woolly material found under the cedar's bark.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means the woolly substance that is in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the challenge by narrowing what part of the cedar is meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The definition 'cedar branch' stands, but it refers to the fluffy fibers inside the branch, not the wood itself. Those fibers could be twisted into a wick, though they burn poorly.

phrases.english: With the woolly substance that is in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in step 14.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the definition to a specific part of the object.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: לכש meant the wooden branch itself.
steps.terutzMaskana: לכש is the woolly fiber beneath the cedar bark.

steps.title: רב יוסף: חוסן is flax tow
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that חוסן means tow, the short leftover fibers of flax.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Nor with חוסן': רב יוסף said it is the tow of flax.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next word on the list, and רב יוסף defines it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tow is the coarse waste that falls off flax when it is combed. רב יוסף says this is what the משנה forbids. This definition is about to be challenged.

keyTerms.meaning: A flax-based material (the meaning is debated)
Tow, the leftover fibers of combed flax

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: נְעוֹרֶת שֶׁל פִּשְׁתָּן.
phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: It is tow of flax.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the second word on the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חוסן is flax tow.

steps.title: אביי's verse shows חוסן is not tow
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a פסוק, 'the חסון shall be as tow,' which implies that חוסן and tow are two different things.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But it is written, 'And the strong one shall be as tow.' This implies that חוסן is not tow!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב יוסף's definition using a פסוק in ישעיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If something 'becomes like' tow, it was not tow to begin with. So the פסוק itself shows that חוסן is a different material from נעורת.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is written (introduces a challenge from a פסוק)

phrases.english: But isn't it written: 'And the ḥason shall be as tow'?
By implication, ḥosen is not tow!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב יוסף's definition in step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's claim that חוסן is נעורת.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק compares חוסן to tow, which shows they are not the same thing.

steps.title: אביי: crushed but uncombed flax
steps.stepSummary: אביי gives his own definition: חוסן is flax that has been crushed but not yet combed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: It is flax that was crushed but not combed.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected רב יוסף's view, אביי offers a new definition of חוסן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Crushed, uncombed flax is still flax, but its fibers are covered in husk and burn poorly. This fits the פסוק, which can now say this flax will turn into tow.
steps.whatToRemember: For חוסן, רב יוסף said it is tow. אביי rejected that from a פסוק and said it is crushed, uncombed flax.

phrases.english: Flax that was crushed and not combed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב יוסף's rejected definition.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Replacement definition that fits the פסוק.

steps.title: שמואל asks the sailors about כלך
steps.stepSummary: שמואל reports that he asked seafarers, and they told him that כלך is called 'כולכא.'
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Nor with כלך': שמואל said, I asked all the seafarers, and they told me its name is כולכא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the third word, כלך, and שמואל identifies it based on what sailors told him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the material was foreign, שמואל asked well-traveled sailors for its current name. He gives a name, כולכא, rather than a description.

keyTerms.meaning: Kulka, the current name of כלך

phrases.english: and they said: its name is kulka.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the third word on the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כלך is called כולכא.

steps.title: רב יצחק בר זעירא: silk cocoon
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר זעירא identifies כלך as גושקרא, the silkworm's cocoon.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יצחק בר זעירא said: It is גושקרא.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives his own identification of כלך.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He describes כלך as the raw silk of the cocoon. No one challenges either view, so both identifications are simply recorded side by side.

phrases.aramaic: רַב יִצְחָק בַּר זְעֵירָא אָמַר: גּוּשְׁקְרָא.
phrases.english: Rav Yitzḥak bar Ze'ira said: It is the silkworm cocoon (gushkera).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives an alternate identification next to שמואל's.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כלך is the silkworm cocoon.

steps.title: רבין identifies כלך as the silk worn by רבנא נחמיה
steps.stepSummary: רבין and אביי see רבנא נחמיה wearing a silk called מטכסא. רבין says this is the כלך from the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין and אביי were sitting before רבנא נחמיה, the brother of the ריש גלותא. רבין saw he was wearing מטכסא silk. רבין said to אביי: This is the כלך that we learned about in the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story in which רבין points to a real piece of silk clothing and says it is the כלך of our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 19-20 gave definitions of כלך from sailors and from רב יצחק בר זעירא. Here רבין offers a hands-on identification: כלך is a specific kind of silk called מטכסא. This becomes the target of the challenge that comes soon.

keyTerms.meaning: The Exilarch, the official leader of Babylonian Jewry
That we learned in a משנה

phrases.english: He saw that he was wearing metaksa (silk).
This is the kalach that we learned in the Mishnah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third identification of כלך, after the ones in steps 19-20
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כלך is the silk called מטכסא

steps.title: אביי gives the local name for this silk
steps.stepSummary: אביי says that in his place this silk is called שירא פרנדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: We call it שירא פרנדא.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on רבין. In his community this garment is called שירא פרנדא, a kind of ordinary silk, so it is not the כלך of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By calling it 'שירא פרנדא', אביי puts this silk in the family of שירא, ordinary silk. If so, it is not כלך. The ברייתא in the next step backs אביי up by listing שיראים and כלך as separate items.

keyTerms.meaning: A type of silk, possibly patterned or fine silk

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבין's identification in step 21 by showing the garment is a kind of שירא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The silk רבין called כלך is known locally as שירא פרנדא
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבין's claim that the מטכסא garment is the כלך of the משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The garment is known as שירא פרנדא, a type of שירא, and שירא is a different material from כלך

steps.title: A ברייתא lists שיראים and כלך separately
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא counts שיראים, כלך, and סריקין as different garments that need ציצית. That suggests כלך is not a kind of שירא, which refutes רבין.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged from a ברייתא: Garments of שיראים, כלך, and סריקין are all obligated in ציצית. This is a refutation of רבין!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to show רבין was wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If כלך were the silk called שירא פרנדא, it would be a type of שירא. The ברייתא, however, lists שיראים and כלך as two separate items. So they must be different materials.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged (from a ברייתא or משנה)
Another type of silk (or combed fabric)

phrases.english: This is a refutation of Ravin!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבין's identification from step 21, using אביי's name from step 22
steps.kashyaTarget: רבין's claim that כלך is the silk called שירא פרנדא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists שיראים and כלך separately, so כלך cannot be a type of שירא
steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is not about שבת wicks at all. It is brought only because it shows that שיראים and כלך are different materials.

steps.title: The גמרא accepts that רבין is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees: it is a refutation.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא admits that the challenge works and that רבין's identification falls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The one word 'תיובתא' is the גמרא's standard way of conceding that an opinion has been fully refuted. Even so, the גמרא will immediately offer another way to read the case.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 23
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבין's identification is refuted by the ברייתא

steps.title: שירא and שירא פרנדא are different materials
steps.stepSummary: Another option: plain שירא is one thing, and שירא פרנדא is something else, so רבין can still be right.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say: שירא is one thing and שירא פרנדא is a separate thing.
steps.whatsHappening: Right after conceding, the גמרא offers another way to defend רבין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that שירא פרנדא is a kind of שירא. Here the גמרא says the shared name is misleading and the two are different materials. That leaves room for שירא פרנדא to be the כלך listed separately in the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say (an alternative answer)

phrases.english: and shira peranda is a separate thing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a way to save רבין despite the concession in step 24
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining a term: the shared name does not mean the same category
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שירא פרנדא is a type of שירא, so it cannot be the כלך listed separately
steps.terutzMaskana: שירא פרנדא is a distinct material from שירא and can be the כלך
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא refutes רבין only if שירא פרנדא is a type of שירא. If it is a separate material, רבין's identification of כלך survives.

steps.title: פתילת האידן is willow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next item in the משנה, פתילת האידן, and explains that it is willow.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And not with פתילת האידן': this is willow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next unfit wick in the משנה and identifies it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new term is defined in one word: אחוינא, willow. The story that follows will show which part of the willow is meant.

keyTerms.meaning: A wick from the 'idan' plant, mentioned in the משנה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new word in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אידן is willow

steps.title: רבין points out willow trees as the אידן
steps.stepSummary: While walking with אביי in the valley of טמרוריתא, רבין sees willow trees and says they are the אידן of the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבין and אביי were walking in the valley of טמרוריתא. They saw some willow trees. רבין said to אביי: This is the אידן that we learned about in the משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story in which רבין points to real willow trees as the אידן. This sets up אביי's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This story backs up the definition of אידן as willow. It also opens a question: how can a tree be used as a wick?

phrases.english: This is the idan that we learned in the Mishnah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the definition from step 26 with a story
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The willow tree is the אידן of the משנה

steps.title: אביי objects that willow is just wood
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבין: a willow is simply wood, so how could anyone make a wick from it?
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: That is just ordinary wood!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back. A משנה about wicks must mean something soft, and a tree looks like plain wood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wicks are made from soft, stringy material. A willow tree seems to have nothing like that, so אביי doubts it can be the אידן.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבין's identification in step 27
steps.kashyaTarget: רבין's claim that the willow is the אידן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Wood cannot be made into a wick, so the משנה cannot be talking about a willow

steps.title: רבין peels the bark and shows the wool-like layer
steps.stepSummary: רבין peels back the bark and shows אביי a soft, wool-like substance between the bark and the wood.
steps.simpleTranslation: He peeled the bark and showed him the wool-like material that is in between.
steps.whatsHappening: רבין answers אביי by showing him, not by arguing. Under the bark there is soft material that could serve as a wick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wick is not made from the wood itself. It is made from the fibrous layer between the bark and the trunk, so the willow can be the אידן after all.

phrases.english: the wool-like substance in between (the bark and the wood).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's objection in step 28
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical demonstration that narrows down which part of the tree is meant
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The willow is only wood and cannot be a wick
steps.terutzMaskana: The wick is made from the soft layer under the willow's bark
steps.whatToRemember: אידן is willow, and the wick comes from the soft, wool-like layer under its bark.

steps.title: פתילת המדבר is mullein
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next item in the משנה, פתילת המדבר, and identifies it as a plant called שברא (mullein).
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And not with פתילת המדבר': this is שברא, mullein.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא identifies another unfit wick material from the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a simple one-word definition: the 'desert wick' is the mullein plant, which does not burn well.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Desert wick', a plant material mentioned in the משנה

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next word in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פתילת המדבר is mullein

steps.title: What is the green moss on the water?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'ולא בירוקה שעל פני המים' from the משנה and asks what this green moss is.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And not with the green moss that is on the water.' What is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the identity of the next item in the משנה. This sets up a proposed answer and its rejection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Many kinds of green growth appear in or on water. The גמרא wants to know which kind could actually be made into a wick, which is why the משנה would need to forbid it.

phrases.english: 'And not with the green moss that is on etc.'
phrases.notes: Short for 'on the surface of the water'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next word in the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the 'green moss on the water'

steps.title: Moss from standing water is rejected because it crumbles
steps.stepSummary: One might suggest the moss found in ditches of standing water, but that moss crumbles and could never become a wick.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is the moss in ditches of standing water, that crumbles apart!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a possible answer and immediately rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only needs to forbid materials that could at least be twisted into a wick. Ditch moss falls apart, so no one would try to use it, and it cannot be what the משנה means.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggestion that will be rejected)
Ditches or pits of standing water

phrases.english: If you say it is the moss of ditches —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests an answer to step 31 and rejects it
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the ירוקה is moss from standing water
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That moss crumbles, so it could never be made into a wick, and the משנה would not need to forbid it

steps.title: רב פפא: it is the moss that grows on ships
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the green moss means the moss that grows on ships, which can be dried and shaped into a wick.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב פפא said: It is the moss of ships.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the accepted answer to the question in step 31.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moss on ships is tougher and holds together, so a person could make a wick from it. Since it still burns poorly, the משנה forbids it.

phrases.english: It is the moss of ships.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the answer rejected in step 32
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ירוקה of the משנה is moss that grows on ships
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה only lists materials that someone could actually make into a wick. That is why the ירוקה is ship moss, not the crumbly moss of ditches.

steps.title: A ברייתא adds wool and hair to the forbidden wicks
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that the Sages added wool and hair to the list of forbidden wicks.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: They added to the list wicks made of wool and of hair.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that lists two more forbidden wick materials that our משנה does not mention. This sets up the next step, which explains why our משנה left them out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה gave a list of materials you may not use as a שבת wick. This ברייתא adds wool and hair to that list. That raises a quiet question: why did our משנה not mention them? The next step answers it.

keyTerms.meaning: They added to them (to the list)

phrases.english: They added to them (the list of forbidden wicks)
those of wool and those of hair.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from defining the משנה's wick materials to a ברייתא that adds more materials.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wool and hair are also forbidden as שבת wicks.

steps.title: Why our משנה did not list wool and hair
steps.stepSummary: Our תנא left out wool and hair because they cannot work as wicks at all: wool shrinks and hair gets scorched.
steps.simpleTranslation: And our תנא did not list them because wool shrinks up and hair gets scorched.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why our משנה did not bother mentioning wool and hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When wool burns it curls up, and when hair burns it singes away. So nobody would ever use them as a wick. Our תנא only listed materials someone might actually try to use, so there was no need to mention these.

keyTerms.meaning: Our תנא (the author of our משנה)

phrases.english: And our Tanna (did not list them because):

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the unspoken question raised by the ברייתא's addition.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical reason for leaving the items out
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our משנה should have listed wool and hair too, and leaving them out looks like a disagreement with the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: There is no disagreement. Wool and hair cannot function as wicks at all, so our תנא had no need to list them.

steps.title: Defining זפת and שעוה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes 'ולא בזפת' from the משנה and explains that זפת is pitch and שעוה is wax.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And not with זפת': זפת is pitch, and שעוה is wax.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next words of the משנה and translates them into everyday Aramaic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said you may not light with זפת or שעוה. The גמרא gives the common names: זפת is זיפתא (pitch, a sticky tree resin), and שעוה is קירותא (wax).
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues going through the משנה phrase by phrase.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: זפת means pitch and שעוה means wax.

steps.title: The משנה switches from wicks to oils
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that up to זפת the משנה lists forbidden wicks, and from there on it lists forbidden oils.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: Up to here are the forbidden wicks; from here on are the forbidden oils.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא shows where the משנה's list changes topic. This sets up a challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה has two lists in a row: things you may not use as a wick, and things you may not use as fuel. The ברייתא says זפת is where the second list starts. So זפת and שעוה are forbidden as fuel, not as wicks.

phrases.english: Up to here, (the Mishnah lists) materials unfit for wicks;
from here on, materials unfit as oils.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining זפת, the גמרא brings a ברייתא about its place in the משנה's structure.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From זפת onward, the משנה lists forbidden fuels, not forbidden wicks.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא needed to say this, since nobody could make a wick out of pitch anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא for teaching something that seems too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pitch is a sticky liquid, not a fiber you can twist into a wick. So of course זפת is on the oil list. Why did the ברייתא need to point it out?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the ברייתא just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא that marks the switch from wicks to oils
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Pitch and similar materials obviously cannot be wicks, so stating that they belong to the oil list adds nothing.

steps.title: The point is about wax
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא was needed for wax. Without it we might think wax is unfit for wicks too. It teaches that wax is forbidden only as fuel, but may be used for wicks.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was needed for wax. You might have said that wax is also not fit for wicks. So it teaches us that it is.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא's real point is about wax, not pitch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wicks were often coated with wax. Since the משנה forbids wax, one might think it is banned even as a wick coating. The ברייתא places wax on the oil list, so it is forbidden only as melted fuel and is fine on a wick.

keyTerms.meaning: It teaches us (that it is not so)

steps.whatToRemember: זפת and שעוה are forbidden only as fuel. Wax is still allowed as part of a wick.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the משנה bans wax completely. It only bans wax as the fuel. Wax may still be used on a wick.
steps.whyThisMatters: In practice, wax-coated wicks may be used for the שבת light, even though wax may not serve as the main fuel.

phrases.english: that it is also not fit for wicks;
so it teaches us (that it is fit for wicks).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies a non-obvious item the teaching was aimed at
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Wax might be forbidden even as a wick coating.
steps.terutzMaskana: Wax is forbidden only as fuel. It is permitted as part of a wick.

steps.title: What tar and wax come from
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר אבין explains that עטרן is the leftover of pitch, and שעוה is the leftover of honey.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר אבין said: Tar is the leftover of pitch. Wax is the leftover of honey.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר אבין explains where two fuel materials come from: עטרן (tar), a by-product of the זפת just discussed, and שעוה (wax), which our משנה listed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When wood is burned to get pitch, a thinner liquid comes out afterward. That liquid is עטרן (tar). In the same way, wax is what is left over from honey in the honeycomb.

phrases.english: Tar is the by-product of pitch.
Wax is the by-product of honey.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining זפת and שעוה, adds where tar (a by-product of pitch) and wax come from.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: עטרן comes from pitch, and שעוה comes from honey.
